stories.title: Disruption as Microsoft battles to fix global outage
stories.summary: Microsoft users are continuing to experience disruption as the tech giant worked to resolve outages impacting some of its most popular services. Monitoring website Downdetector first showed a spike in users reporting problems with Microsoft Teams in Ireland and the UK at around 6.15pm yesterday. Microsoft said that it was not aware of any "malicious activity" behind the hours-long disruption of its Outlook services. "As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident. We will continue to treat this incident with urgency and priority until full resolution," Microsoft said. The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Microsoft Outlook. Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories were hit, outage tracker Downdetector reported. A map posted by Downdetector showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

stories.title: Agreement reached on EU Budget for 2027 - Tánaiste
stories.summary: Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris said an agreement has been reached on the European Union's Budget for 2027. The deal was agreed in the early hours of this morning following negotiations in Brussels, he said in a statement. Negotiations in the Belgium capital were chaired by Ireland as part of its EU Presidency. The 2027 budget is the final annual budget under the EU's current seven-year funding framework. The agreement provides for €199.7 billion in commitments and €211.5b in payments, said Mr Harris. He said €710.1m will be left available under the EU's spending limits to give "governments, organisations and communities greater certainty as they plan for the year ahead".

stories.title: Frasers tightens grip at Hugo Boss with new CEO pick
stories.summary: Frasers Group executive David Epstein will succeed Daniel Grieder as CEO of Hugo Boss from January 1, 2027, the German fashion group has said, cementing the British retailer's influence over the company. The leadership transition comes after Frasers Group, already Hugo Boss' largest shareholder, took majority control of the company in October by raising its stake above 50%, months after an unsuccessful €2 billion takeover bid. The move also follows a series of leadership changes at Hugo Boss this year. The company's CFO Yves Müller departed and was replaced by Ivica Maric in October, while chief sales officer Oliver Timm is set to leave at the end of November, the company announced earlier this week. In September, Hugo Boss also named Michael Murray, chief executive of Frasers Group, as chairman of its supervisory board. "With strong foundation in place, I am convinced that now is the right time for me to step down and hand over to the next generation of leadership," Grieder said in a statement. Grieder had recently expressed optimism about working with the new chairman, citing constructive dialogue with Frasers Group after the third-quarter earnings call, during which Hugo Boss lowered its full-year forecast.

stories.title: Pope Leo draws huge crowds at Argentina's holiest shrine
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has drawn vast crowds to Argentina's holiest shrine on the final day of his visit before he departs for Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary. Authorities said over three million people packed the streets around the Basilica of Lujan, with some climbing fences, barriers, trees and lampposts for a glimpse of the pontiff. Crowds chanted "thank you Leo!" to the 71-year-old pope, who is on a 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru less than a month after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The stop at Lujan was the emotional centerpiece of Leo's first visit to Argentina, where his predecessor Francis never managed to return home as pope. "Thank you, Argentina, for welcoming me with open arms," he said as he bid farewell to the thronging crowd, which was the largest he drew during his visit to the country. Throughout his stay in Argentina, Pope Leo has pointedly demanded a more inclusive economy and better protections for the vulnerable, comments widely interpreted as criticism of aid-slashing President Javier Milei.

stories.title: Preview: Ireland U21s set for huge Finland play-off clash
stories.summary:
UEFA European Under-21 European Championship Play-Off first leg
Finland v Republic of Ireland, Tammelan Stadion, Tampere, 4.15pm (Irish time) It's over four years since the Republic of Ireland Under-21s suffered European Championships play-off pain in Tel Aviv, losing to Israel in a penalty shootout. That's as close as Jim Crawford has come to leading the country to a Euros at the grade for the first time. Crawford has always insisted his primary job is to help players break into the senior team, but it's understandably an itch he's desperate to scratch. He has endured a huge amount of frustration since succeeding Stephen Kenny in April 2020. After the disappointment in Israel, Crawford's side went into the Euro 2025 campaign searching for redemption. Ireland were seconds away from scalping Italy in Turner's Cross only for Wilfred Gnonto to pinch a point for the visitors at the death. In the home clash with Norway, a controversial Andreas Schjelderup equaliser deep into stoppage time denied Ireland victory and a place in the play-offs. They subsequently travelled to Italy for their final group game needing to win. They drew 1-1, the Italians taking top spot and Norway nabbing the play-off place because of their better head-to-head record.
stories.rssSummary: The Republic of Ireland Under-21s are in Finland for the first leg of their European Championship play-off, looking to take another step towards what would a historic tournament qualification.

stories.title: Comfort TV show picks for navigating your twenties
stories.summary: When it comes to selecting a show to re-watch, like many people I find myself drawn to the comfort TV classics of the 2000s, writes Caoimhe Mahon. Shows like One Tree Hill, 90210, The O.C. or The Vampire Diaries are often queued in my streaming list, ready for the inevitable re-watch. stories.title: Éanna Hardwicke honoured in Cork as film festival opens
stories.summary: Cork actor Éanna Hardwicke has been honoured on the opening night of this year's Cork International Film Festival. The Glanmire-raised actor was presented with the Honorary Puttnam Award for his contribution to cinema. Accepting his award at the MTU Cork School of Music, the Saipan star said: "I fell in love with acting in Saturday classes inside in the South Parish Community Centre. "As a teenager, under the outstanding teachers at the MTU Cork School of Music, I realised this is what I wanted to spend my life doing. "I feel blessed to have grown up in this city and to have gotten the rich theatre education I did here. "To return to the South Parish, to the MTU Cork School of Music, a building that has a very special resonance to me, and to receive this Honorary Puttnam Award, named after David Puttnam, Cork International Film Festival Patron - who has played such a seismic role in art and cinema in this city - is a great honour.

stories.title: What to wear on a winter weekend away
stories.summary: Packing clothes for a weekend away can be difficult to consolidate at the best of times, but when it coincides with the colder months, squeezing bulky knitwear, heavy coats and the inevitable extra pair of shoes into a weekend bag without sacrificing anything can feel impossible. The trends for autumn/winter 2026 bring an abundance of maximalist textures from faux fur to fringe, meaning the season's most fashionable pieces aren’t necessarily the easiest to pack. Marks and Spencer's head of creative styling Francesca Zedda says the secret to a stylish winter weekend wardrobe isn’t about how much you bring, but how well everything works together. "The best weekend wardrobe isn’t about packing lots of statement pieces. It’s about choosing well-cut, hardworking styles that feel current but can be worn in several different ways," she tells the Press Association. So, whether you’re heading off for a countryside retreat or a European city break, here’s what to pack for a winter weekend away – and how to make the most of limited suitcase space. Before thinking about individual outfits, starting with a handful of pieces that can be worn in different combinations is what Zedda recommends.

stories.title: Taoiseach to host informal meeting of EU leaders
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin will host an informal meeting of EU leaders in Dublin this morning following yesterday's European Political Community summit. Leaders will assess the latest update by US envoys to Russia following their meeting with Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel last night. Following the meeting with Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who had met Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier in Moscow, Mr Zelensky said European negotiators will take part in talks directly with Ukraine-Russia delegations in US-led talks in Abu Dhabi next week. While talks took place in the UAE this week, European officials did not participate directly. After being briefed by the US envoys, Mr Zelensky said Europeans will take part in the next talks rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines. "We cannot conclude this deal without Europeans being at the table," Mr Kushner said alongside the Ukrainian leader in Casement Aerodrome.

stories.title: Cartier-owner Richemont quarterly sales beat estimates
stories.summary: Cartier-owner Richemont has today reported a faster-than expected quarterly sales increase, helped by continued demand for its jewellery and bumper growth in the US and Japan. The company, which also owns Swiss watch brands Piaget and IWC, said its sales rose by 13% when measured in constant currencies to €5.95 billion in the three months to the end of September. The figure beat analyst forecasts for €5.89 billion in a consensus compiled by Visible Alpha. Although a slowdown from the 20% growth rate in the prior quarter, the figure showed the resilience of Richemont's largely jewellery-based business and a strong performance in the US, Japan and Europe, where sales increased by 15% or more. The Swiss-based company, which makes brooches, earrings and necklaces under the Cartier, Buccellati, Van Cleef & Arpels and Vhernier brands, has bucked the trend in a struggling luxury industry thanks to its higher exposure to jewellery, with its jewellery brands accounting for about 75% of its revenues. Sales of Richemont's jewellery unit grew 14% in the quarter, while those of its specialist watchmakers division rose 12%.

stories.title: Ryan: 'We're not thinking about South Africa'
stories.summary: James Ryan insists Ireland are solely focused on Fiji, despite a crunch tie with South Africa looming next week. Ireland host the Fijians on Saturday night in the second game of their Nations Championship window, before welcoming the Springboks to Dublin on 21 November. Next week's meeting with the world champions will be something of a revenge mission after last year's 24-13 defeat at the Aviva, where the Springboks humiliated the Irish scrum, while Ryan was one of five Ireland players carded, picking up a 20-minute red card in the first half. stories.title: The Floating World by Ben Eastham - read an extract
stories.summary: We present an extract from The Floating World, the debut novel by Ben Eastham. On a remote island in the Aegean, a billionaire named Morel is building a refuge for the super-rich from the chaos consuming the outside world. When a struggling journalist is hired to work on the spectacular exhibition that will inaugurate this exclusive new utopia, he jumps at the chance to restart a career that stopped with the death of his wife. Yet he comes to suspect that beneath the dazzling surface of this collaboration between art and power run currents of real violence... Ben Eastham's novel is a dystopia, satire and Bildungsroman, steeped in ancient mythology and contemporary politics. Yesterday I planted a tree in the garden. A magnolia, to be precise, having fond memories of the flowers that used to enliven South London in spring. At the beginning of every April, having waited through winter for it to blossom, Cora would reward the tree at the end of our street with a kiss that, like sunlight, served to accelerate the process. She had a gift for these things. I do not, and am already worried for my sapling. It stands this morning in a circle of ground painted white by a frost that I might have seen coming. The stream in the valley beyond is so bright in the low sun that I fear it has frozen over; the long black girders stretching from isolated trees fix the landscape in place. Nothing about this morning seems conducive to new life. Should I heat some water to defrost the soil in which the tree is planted? Should I shelter it beneath one of the tarpaulins covering stacks of peat by the shed? Probably I should go down to the village to use the wifi, but I don't want to be ambushed by the news. The woman at the garden centre had betrayed no such anxieties. Just find a spot with plenty of light, she’d advised, and the tree will take care of itself. Aoife was the only employee still coming into work, she told me as we walked through an arbour threaded with honeysuckle, payments not having cleared since the crash. But she had nothing better to do than to keep the plants alive through the winter, until normality resumed.

stories.title: How early perimenopause led an Irish woman to an Autism diagnosis
stories.summary: Diagnosed with severe Dyslexia and Dyspraxia from a young age, Hannah Daly has long been passionate about advocating for those with different needs. Representing Dublin at the Rose of Tralee competition in 2008, she spoke passionately about her "challenging" experience in school, both with the lack of educational support and the bullying that followed. Following her appearance, she was met with a flood of messages from those with similar struggles. The experience led her to run a theatre company for actors with disabilities and facilitate workshops, courses and seminars in self-advocacy and drama for adults and children. Although she already had a Degree in the Performing Arts, her work in theatre inspired her to return to third-level education. Working around her own learning differences, she qualified as an Occupational Therapist in 2013 before completing a post-graduate degree in Sensory Integration. Specialising in Autism, ADHD, Dyslexia, Dyspraxia and OCD, Daly has worked with neurodivergent adults and children for most of her career. All of which made her multi-neurodivergent diagnosis all the more surprising. "I didn't see it in myself because we didn't see it in girls," she explains. "I would have had some girls on my caseload but, predominantly, a large proportion of the girls would also have had an intellectual disability or mental health challenges."

stories.title: PSNI officers fired over 'utterly despicable' behaviour
stories.summary: Two PSNI officers have been dismissed for what a police oversight body has described as "utterly despicable" behaviour towards vulnerable people they had been sent to help. Police Officer A took videos and pictures of people who were drunk, had reported crimes, or were considered at risk of self-harm, without their knowledge and shared them. In total, 18 people had images taken in places like homes, hospitals and police vehicles. Some were then shared on WhatsApp accompanied with sexualised and demeaning commentary. In one case a woman with complex needs was videoed by the officer in her bedroom during which highly inappropriate sexual comments were made. "Almost all of the people affected by these actions were vulnerable, some extremely so," said Police Ombudsman Jacqui Durkin.

stories.title: AIB announces doubling of green lending target at COP31
stories.summary: AIB said it is increasing its green and transition lending target, doubling it from €30 billion to €60 billion by 2030. The announcement was made by the bank's chief executive Colin Hunt at the COP31 climate change ⁠talks in Turkey. AIB said it has already deployed €28 billion in cumulative green and transition funds since 2019, which it said represents 93% of its existing €30 billion target. The bank loaned out €6.3 billion in green lending last year, accounting for 43% of new lending. Another €5.3 billion has been deployed in the first nine months of this year. AIB said its increased targets will supports its customers, from funding large scale renewable energy infrastructure and energy efficient homes to helping businesses and farmers reduce their environmental footprints. AIB CEO Colin Hunt said that banks have a critical role in turning climate ambition into practical action.

stories.title: Amond wins SWI Player of the Month award for October
stories.summary: Padraig Amond has been named the SSE Airtricity/Soccer Writers Ireland Player of the Month for October. The 38 year-old in-form striker topped the nationwide poll with 72 votes to oust second placed Patrick McClean of Derry City on 55 votes with Shamrock Rovers star Graham Burke in third place on 27 votes. Amond came up short to McClean's Derry in last Sunday's Club Orange FAI Cup final. The veteran Blues front man continues to inspire his team and another stellar month saw him haul himself into contention for the Golden Boot with five goals and an assist including a spectacular bicycle kick against Galway United. He also scored his 50th goal for the club since his return to Ireland three years ago after an extensive career in the UK. Amond has now made over 800 career appearances and he notched 18 goals this season as Graham Coughlan’s team avoided the dreaded drop and dove-tailed that achievement with a superb run all the way to the FAI Cup decider.

stories.title: 5 takeaways from Dublin's EPC summit
stories.summary: Following a day of hectic diplomatic activity around Dublin's Convention Centre, reporter Harry Manning takes a look at five key takeaways from the ninth European Political Community summit. There was certainly a sense that there had been a significant shift, maybe even towards one of optimism, in regards to Europe's role in peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. Earlier this week, US envoy Jared Kushner said the EU must be involved in the talks in order to guarantee the future security of Europe. Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky demanded that Europe became a "regular part" of Ukraine talks - a sentiment echoed by a number of leaders under the roof of the Convention Centre. However, with the question of Europe taking a seat at the table now seemingly answered, attention turned to which of the European leaders should be sitting in the chair. The Taoiseach said it may not even need to be a single representative, but perhaps a dream team of European spokespeople.

stories.title: McManus fulfils her Dunloy dream after long journey
stories.summary: When the final whistle went on Saturday at the end of a pulsating AIB Ulster senior club camogie final, Dunloy's Aileen McManus (née Martin) was where she always wanted to be – on the field celebrating with the team-mates closest to her. "It's something I have wanted all my life and to get game time, it might have been just five or six minutes at the end, that was just the icing on the cake," she reflected after the hard fought 1-10 to 0-11 victory over Clonduff of Down. "I’m so delighted for all the girls, for the whole team. They have the chance to get more days like today. I thought my days had passed. It has taken me 22 years to get here." Aileen Martin believed she would have plenty of days like Saturday when she came into the Dunloy senior team back in 2004 as a 15-year-old. The year before, she had watched her heroes win their second Ulster club title. The first came nine years earlier and the Antrim title had come to the village five times during those nine seasons. She wasn’t too annoyed about losing her first final to Rossa in Corrigan Park that summer. "I was probably just pleased to get playing alongside the likes of Elaine Dowds, Oonagh Elliott, Edel Mason (Ciara Mageean’s aunt), Anne McKee.

stories.title: Nvidia ex-CEO to testify before US Senate committee
stories.summary: US politicians have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote on X. Mr Scott said he was requesting Mr Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with Mr Huang on 1 December by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Mr Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted on Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related.

stories.title: Farrell backs McNabney to make his mark on Test rugby
stories.summary: Andy Farrell believes Ulster's James McNabney is ready to make the step up to Test level, after naming the 23-year-old in his squad for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Fiji. The Ulster back row is in line to win his first cap against Jake White's side, with the former Ireland U20 star among the replacements on Saturday night at the Aviva. Had it not been for injury, McNabney could already be capped at Test level. He enjoyed a breakout season for Ulster in 2024/25, playing 17 games in all competitions, and was named as a development player for the 2025 Six Nations, before suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury in Ireland camp ahead of the summer Tests against Georgia and Portugal. That injury sidelined the Ballymena man for all of last season, but after getting back on the pitch with Ulster for the start of this season, he is now in line to make his Ireland debut. "I think it's a brilliant story," Farrell said of the new cap.

stories.title: Small islands aim to use remittances in climate battle
stories.summary: A group of small island states aims to create a fund backed by a charge on money that islanders receive from abroad to eventually raise around $3 billion (€2.69bn) a year for projects to make their nations less vulnerable to climate change. That would exceed the roughly $2bn in international public adaptation finance they received in 2021 to 2022, according to a 2025 study by non-profit research group the Climate Policy Initiative. Country representatives meeting until the end of next week in the Mediterranean city of Antalya in Turkey for COP31 climate talks are trying to agree ways to increase funding for adaptation to a warming world. Representatives of Small Island Developing States, or SIDS, have decided they cannot wait for the long-running international debate on financing to deliver more help. "We decided that there had to be a way that we can guarantee more reliable sources of funding for the islands," Antigua and Barbuda's UN ambassador Walton Webson said. "We cannot rely solely on development assistance again." The SIDS grouping brings together island nations in the Pacific, the Caribbean and the Atlantic, Indian Ocean, and South China Sea that are particularly vulnerable to the impact of rising sea levels as the planet warms.

stories.title: Nations Lge: Kane scores in record cap, Italy stun France
stories.summary: England captain Harry Kane marked his record-breaking 126th cap with a 92nd international goal as the skipper's spot-kick sealed a 2-1 win over Croatia and set up a Nations League shootout in Spain. The irrepressible 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley, where the Bayern Munich sharpshooter’s Ballon d’Or triumph was celebrated along with his landmark appearance. Kane became the most capped Englishman in history, having last month equalled the record held by Peter Shilton, who was on hand to make a pre-match presentation to the star along with the Prince of Wales. The striker looked like he would be denied a customary goal on this special night as Croatia defended diligently before capitalising on a second-half error to cancel out Morgan Rogers’ opener. Petar Sucic pounced on a poor Jarell Quansah header, but the England defender quickly won a penalty that Kane slammed home as the nation’s all-time scorer netted in a fifth successive game. Thomas Tuchel’s men had already effectively secured qualification for March’s Nations League quarter-finals before this match, but Thursday’s victory rubberstamped it and kept hopes alive of winning Group A3 heading into Sunday’s trip to leaders Spain.

stories.title: Pope says Church must make amends to abuse victims
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV yesterday met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru including some linked to the once powerful and now disbanded Catholic society, Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pope is on a nostalgic return to the nation he calls his "homeland" and knows the abuse scandal well from the nearly two decades he worked in Peru as a missionary and bishop. Pope Leo spent more than an hour with the victims, meeting "each person individually, listening to their stories of suffering and their pain" and "thanked them for their invaluable testimony", the Vatican said. Together, "they reflected on how to foster a shift in mindset - by listening to victims, seeking the truth, pursuing paths toward healing and committing to the creation of safe environments", it said. Sodalitium Christianae Vitae (SCV), a lay society founded in the 1970s that was widespread in Latin America, was shut down in 2025 by Pope Leo's predecessor, Pope Francis, after years of allegations of sexual, physical and psychological abuse, as well as corruption. Before he was elected Pope Leo, Robert Francis Prevost was the bishop designated to hear from SCV victims, who said he was supportive of their claims.

stories.summary: Finn Harps' approach to use MacCumhaill Park, the home of Donegal GAA, as its home base during the 2027 League of Ireland First Division season is set to be decided by a club membership vote. Sean MacCumhaills GAA held an "information evening" on the matter on Thursday evening with the logistics of facilitating Harps’ request discussed. New Harps owner Freddy Gonzalez is keen to start major upgrade works at Finn Park, and correspondence was recently sent to their GAA neighbours inquiring about the possibility of sharing their ground with major redevelopment work set to begin at Finn Park. MacCumhaills GAA club subsequently contacted members on Tuesday afternoon to give notice of their own specially convened meeting to weigh up the proposition. MacCumhaills explained that this would be an information evening and that it was "not proposed to make any formal decision at this meeting". Christian Happel, Harps’ new CEO, was in attendance at Thursday evening’s gathering in the Sean MacCumhaills clubhouse. It was explained that Harps would be prepared to hire a full-time grounds person if the vote did fall in their favour.

stories.title: Europe must be at table for Ukraine peace talks - Kushner
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoy Jared Kushner said Europeans would be at the table for the next talks with Russia on ending the war, after Washington's representatives met Vladimir Putin. After being briefed by the US envoys at Casement Aerodrome in Dublin, Mr Zelensky said Europeans will take part in the next talks rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines. "We cannot conclude this deal without Europeans being at the table," Mr Kushner said, speaking alongside the Ukrainian leader in Baldonnel. US envoy Steve Witkoff and Mr Kushner stopped in Dublin after a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, following on from trilateral peace talks in the UAE earlier this week. Mr Kushner said they had had a "very detailed and productive" meeting with Mr Putin and his negotiating team. "We had very, very good discussions on a lot of fronts," Mr Kushner said.

stories.title: Óiche na hÓige events to take place nationwide
stories.summary: A celebration of youth work in communities will take place across Ireland tonight as part of Oíche na hÓige (Youth Night) as youth clubs and services are set to open to the wider community. The Department of Education and Youth initiative, now in its second year seeks to celebrate members of youth clubs and groups, youth workers and volunteers. Events are being delivered in partnership with Education and Training Boards, the National Youth Council of Ireland and the youth work sector. Several hundred events will take place in villages, towns and cities. Some events are invitation only; others are open to the public. Foróige Volunteer Development Manager Denis O'Brien said the initiative is based on Culture Night with the organisation set to host more than 200 events. Mr O'Brien said young people are given a platform to showcase and celebrate their work, volunteers and staff are given recognition, and the community is provided with a greater sense of what young people are doing to make their community a better place.

stories.title: Tenant shoots building manager, wounds four in Washington
stories.summary: A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighbourhood of Washington. Local media has reported that the shooter died after an apparent ⁠self-inflicted ‌gunshot wound. The shooting, which occurred about 2km north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation's capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead. Jeffery Carroll, Washington's interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, aged 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment. The man, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager in a gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, and then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Mr Carroll said. He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four.

stories.title: United look to wrap up Pochettino deal as Carrick sacked
stories.summary: Manchester United are working to finalise a deal to appoint United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino after sacking Michael Carrick. The former Red Devils midfielder was dismissed on Thursday morning as confirmation finally arrived of what had been an open secret since the start of the week. Carrick led United to third place last season, having stepped in following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious January exit, but the head coach paid the price for overseeing the club's worst start to a campaign since 1986. Sunday's wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa leaves them in the relegation zone and the 18th-placed side are now working to wrap up a deal to bring Pochettino back to the Premier League. A framework had already been established for the former Argentina international's appointment, with talks understood to be progressing between the Old Trafford club and Pochettino's employers US Soccer. Pochettino has a release clause - worth a reported $10m (€9m) - and the relevant parties are seeking to provide clarity before the USA's Nations League quarter-final first leg against Haiti on Saturday.

stories.title: Beirne captains Ireland, Timoney starts at 8 v Fiji
stories.summary: Tadhg Beirne will captain Ireland in Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Fiji, while Nick Timoney has won the race to start at number 8 in the absence of Sean Jansen. Head coach Andy Farrell has made seven changes to the side that defeated Argentina 42-12 last week, with Joe McCarthy and Hugo Keenan seemingly rested ahead of next week's clash with South Africa. With Dan Sheehan injured, Munster's Tadhg Beirne captains Ireland for just the second time, having skippered the side in their Nations Championship win against Japan in the summer, and he's joined in the second row by James Ryan, who replaces McCarthy. Rónan Kelleher replaces Sheehan at hooker, while Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong continue at prop. Timoney moves across from flanker to number 8 this weekend. While he has never started in that position for Ireland, the 31-year-old played a large portion of his rugby there for Ulster earlier in his career. Josh van der Flier returns to the starting team at openside flanker, after featuring from the bench a week ago, while Ryan Baird continues on the blindside, after an impressive return last week.

With Dan Sheehan injured, Munster's Tadhg Beirne captains Ireland for just the second time, having skippered the side in their Nations Championship win against Japan in the [[samhradh|summer]], and he's joined in the second row by James Ryan, who replaces McCarthy. Rónan Kelleher replaces Sheehan at hooker, while Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong continue at prop. Timoney moves across from flanker to number 8 this [[deireadh seachtaine|weekend]]. While he has never started in that position for Ireland, the 31-year-old played a large portion of his rugby there for Ulster earlier in his career. Josh van der Flier returns to the starting [[foireann|team]] at openside flanker, after featuring from the [[binse|bench]] a week ago, while Ryan Baird continues on the blindside, after an impressive return last week.
